description:
Give the event log one torn-line rule on both sides: every append lands at the end of the last newline-terminated line, and the parser ignores a final line without a terminating newline and rejects any other malformed line.

## Background

The finalizer appends at the captured log length and, when the log ends in an unterminated final line, prefixes a separator newline (`compose_events`, `captured_log_end`, `crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs`). That turns the fragment into a permanent malformed middle line. To avoid corrupting the log, the finalizer refuses every append over an unterminated, unparseable final line unless the mutation writes a profile marker (`MutationError::UncertifiedTornTail`). `finalize_audit_append` shares the path. Both backends already apply an event append at its offset and truncate to the offset plus its bytes (`storage/redo_apply.rs`, `storage/memory.rs`), and the end-of-log probe already holds the final line (@/issue/c88822a5/decision/D-1). `test_profile_application_does_not_mark_valid_unterminated_event_as_torn` in `commands/profile.rs` pins that a complete valid unterminated record is preserved; under this rule the next append overwrites it, since only a foreign writer can leave one: a crash mid-apply leaves a redo record the next session completes.

`domain::parse_known_events` (`domain/event_log.rs`) iterates `contents.lines()`, which cannot see a terminator. It skips a malformed line only when the next line is a profile-lifecycle record whose `isolated_torn_tail` is true (`certifies_preceding_torn_tail`). An unknown tag is an error naming its line (`EventLogError::UnknownTag`), owned by `test_read_events_rejects_unknown_tags_and_malformed_records` (`storage/issue_store_conformance.rs`) and pinned by the failure levers; that stays.

`event_log_drift` (`validation/record_fidelity.rs`) feeds each newline-stripped line to the parser, so under the new rule every line would be an ignored unterminated final line, and it scans the log a second time as raw `serde_json::Value` for ids. `read_events` (`storage/json.rs`) takes `.events.lock` shared, so `jit events` waits on writers, against @/charter/D-22; with this rule a partly appended line is simply ignored.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The length a mutation reads from the event log is its committed length: the end of its last newline-terminated line, which the end-of-log probe determines. Every event append, `finalize_audit_append` included, is positioned at that length and writes no separator newline. The rustdoc of `compose_events` and `captured_log_end` and the offset tests say committed length.
- [hard] REQ-02: No mutation refuses to append over an unterminated final line, and a finalizer unit test shows that an append over one starts at that line's offset and leaves a log every line of which is newline-terminated.
- [hard] REQ-03: `parse_known_events` ignores a final line that has no terminating newline, skips blank lines, and returns an error naming the line for a line whose tag is unknown and for any other line that is not a well-formed event record.
- [hard] REQ-04: No reader certifies a malformed line by the record that follows it, `certifies_preceding_torn_tail` no longer exists, and one parser unit test owns the rule: an unterminated final line is ignored, a malformed middle line is rejected.
- [hard] REQ-05: `event_log_drift` passes each line to the parser with its terminator, takes event ids from the parsed events and parses no line as raw JSON, and `test_event_log_drift_reports_a_line_that_does_not_reproduce` still passes.
- [hard] REQ-06: `read_events` reads the log without `.events.lock`.
title: Event-log readers ignore an unterminated final line that the next append overwrites
